# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with four package scaffolds (initial commit).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen quarter range, downloaded as the baseline | R1, §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | Requests: about 2 per quarter (listing + master.idx). At most about 272 requests, or about 90 s at 3 req/s (§4.8), if the range starts at 1993 Q1. Bytes measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | R2, §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files per year plus listings, so seconds per run at 3 req/s. Catch-up from the handoff date measured at Stage 2 |
| O3 | Downloaded indexes turned into a validated, normalized filing-index dataset in Parquet | R3, §4.4, §4.6 | A | 3 | Parse time and peak memory per quarter measured by Stage 1 (§7 step 4) |
| O4 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs executing on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Log Analytics) | R4, §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure dollars: no estimate until resource sizes are chosen (§4.8). Measured at Stage 3 |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher, differing only in which sources they select | R5, §4.1 | A | 5 | No material cost |
| O6 | A parser change re-run over stored original bytes, with no new download | R6, §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Raw retention is about the baseline's byte volume plus daily files. Measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read periodically, with additions and field changes applied to the catalog | R7, §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | Weekly refresh of every supported quarter: about 136 requests, or about 45 s at 3 req/s. Only changed hashes are transformed |
| O8 | All SEC traffic through one downloader under one request budget, however many workers run | R8, §4.3 | A | 8 | No material cost |
| O9 | Readers find the current dataset through one versioned manifest per quarter behind one active pointer | R9, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | One retained Parquet generation per quarter per publication. Size measured at Stage 4 |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only through an approved, hash-bound closed-quarter replacement | R10, §4.4 | A | 10 | Your time per approval. Frequency unknown until Stage 5 runs reconciliation |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target held as reviewed configuration values | R11, §4.8 | A | 11 | No material cost |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Quarterly baseline to Parquet
      Objective: Download real archived quarterly indexes for a chosen range and publish them as canonical Parquet, run locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: A SEC User-Agent identity and a quarter range, recorded per §4.8 and §7 step 1. Nothing else is built.
      Produces: A downloader and parser for quarterly master indexes, sec-index-v1 Parquet for the range, and specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in the real range has its original master.idx retained with SHA-256 and byte count, or appears in a failure report. O3 — rows for those quarters are in sec-index-v1 Parquet with per-quarter row counts, and malformed rows are refused with line and reason. Cost — the findings file records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and the observed request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: deployment: Stage 3; manifests and traceability: Stage 4; point-in-time generations: Stage 4; scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily continuation on shared code
      Objective: Ingest real daily indexes from a handoff date through the present, using the Stage 1 downloader, parser and publisher.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1 Produces. A daily handoff date (§4.8).
      Produces: Daily discovery and catch-up that share code with backfill, and Parquet covering the handoff date to the present
      Exit: O2 — a run after a simulated missed period ingests every listed, unprocessed daily file, including across a quarter boundary, and reports pending gaps and no_new_sources separately. O5 — backfill and daily runs import one downloader, parser and publisher, and differ only in source selection.
      Leaves out: deployment: Stage 3; manifests and traceability: Stage 4; scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Azure platform
      Objective: Run the backfill and daily commands as ADF-orchestrated Container Apps Jobs, with files in ADLS, control state in Table Storage and logs in Log Analytics.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stage 2 Produces. The ADR accepted, and environment and deployment settings recorded (§7 step 1).
      Produces: Versioned infrastructure, a pinned worker image, and an isolated environment where ADF starts and polls jobs
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, a manual ADF run of one archived quarter and one published daily index completes, with matching worker result files in ADLS and logs in Log Analytics. Production triggers stay disabled.
      Leaves out: scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Replay and versioned publication
      Objective: Add source manifests and traceability, replay from retained bytes, and publish quarters as generations behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 Produces
      Produces: Source, snapshot, processing and publication manifests, point-in-time generations per quarter, and the active pointer in Table Storage
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds a quarter from ADLS with SEC access disabled and yields no duplicate logical records. O9 — readers resolve each quarter through its active pointer to a manifest file list, and an injected crash before the pointer update leaves the prior generation readable.
      Leaves out: scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, apply additions and field updates, and gate withdrawals on hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4 Produces
      Produces: A reconciliation command, change reports per generation, and withdrawal approval records
      Exit: O7 — a manual reconciliation run on the isolated environment refreshes every supported quarter, skips unchanged hashes and publishes recorded additions and updates. O10 — a corrected closed-quarter fixture that removes keys stays awaiting_approval until an approval names its source hash, and open-quarter absence withdraws nothing.
      Leaves out: scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Shared request budget
      Objective: Put every SEC request from backfill, daily and reconciliation under one Storage-backed lease and one rate budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 5 Produces
      Produces: A single SEC request issuer across all pipelines, with daily work taking priority
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation jobs on the isolated environment never exceed the configured rate in combined request logs, and a lease-loss test shows no overlapping request issuers.
      Leaves out: scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduled operation and hardening
      Objective: Hold defaults as reviewed configuration, complete the full validation suite, alerts and runbooks, run the baseline campaign, and enable scheduling.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 6 Produces
      Produces: The full validation suite (§6), alerts, runbooks (§8), the release record, and enabled daily and reconciliation triggers
      Exit: O11 — every §4.8 setting is validated before any network request and changes only through configuration review. The full validation suite and integration tests pass. The baseline campaign and daily catch-up report no silent gaps. Observed scheduled runs are recorded with their reports and alerts (§7 steps 6–9).
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O11), with evidence per verdict. Also list as unmet any of R1–R11 that no outcome's Spec cell cites. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage, or as a conscious deferral with a written why.
